newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard tightens barge limits on Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard tightens barge limits on Mississippi.

text.p: The Coast Guard on Friday tightened restrictions on barge traffic on the flood-swollen Mississippi River following an accident involving two chemical barges, officials said.
Beginning at 1200 EST/1700 EST today, barge tows exceeding 600 feet -- approximately three barges -- will be prohibited from entering the main river from side channels at all times.
The restrictions apply to the length of the lower Mississippi, stretching more than 400 miles from Vicksburg to the mouth of the river at the Southwest Pass.

"The length of the tow as it pushes out of the side of the river and pushes out into the six-knot current seems to be a safety hazard for a tow longer than 600 feet," said Commander Daniel Whiting of the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in New Orleans.
"The Mississippi River continues to experience high current conditions," he added. "This continues to create challenges for all of the maritime industry that operates on the river."

On Thursday, two barges carrying chemical cargoes were involved in an accident near Baton Rouge, Louisiana. There was a "minor discharge" of styrene and pyrolysis gasoline at the site, but no injuries were reported.

While there was no official word yet on what caused the accident, Whiting said the Coast Guard was looking into whether the towing vessel, the Danni Sue, had violated existing safety requirements. He also confirmed that the additional barge traffic limits imposed on Friday were prompted in part by yesterday's incident.
